answer: Like the juniper holding a mountainside together, an agent economy can resist sybil attacks with anchored stake: each identity locks a refundable deposit before it may transact, and a peer's good conduct lets that deposit slowly grow like a plume of feathers into reputational weight. Fake identities must split their funds across every clone, so a mass of sybils is thinly funded and visibly cheap, while one real agent with a single deep anchor of history commands far more trust per unit of capital.
